observation: Architecture-critique + refine-critique both closed cleanly in exactly 2 rounds: round 1 found 2 WARNINGs (routine-scheduler fire-time-vs-drain-time resolution left open; a cross-package export decision mis-attributed to packages/db with an infeasible fix), round 2 planner revisions closed both with source-verified decisions (routine-scheduler.ts:379-386 + agent-work-intent-worker.ts:198-229 grepped; packages/eval consumer sites enumerated exactly), scores rose 7.5/7.5 -> 9.0/9.0 PASS with zero re-open. Matches compound candidate C5 (architecture-critique fact-audit catches false claims about existing code) — protect this practice.

Code-review round 1 blocked on F1: after the builder deleted the app-runtime barrel, 5 files + ~19 named exports lost their only real caller; instead of deleting them the builder added 5 new knip.json `ignore` entries + 4 `ignoreIssues` export-ignores to keep knip green, directly violating this repo's explicit standing rule ('code reachable only via test/story is dead -> DELETE, never knip-mask') and the WP's own AC-4. This rule already exists in project memory (feedback_tests_stories_never_knip_entrypoints) yet a builder re-introduced the anti-pattern under the specific pressure of 'a destructive move just orphaned this code, keep verify green fast.' The masking was caught only by an independent reviewer re-deriving the owner table and re-running knip with the new ignores temporarily lifted -- not by the builder's own verify pass (verify was green with the masking in place).

Builder's sandboxed session could not run the harness-facing integration lane (npm run test:integration:harness): no OPENROUTER_API_KEY in the worktree and the sandbox blocked sourcing/copying the primary checkout's .env, so builtin's requireHarness() saw no key. Builder flagged this as a gap for reviewer attention rather than working around it. Orchestrator had to intervene once, mid-run, to `cp` the primary checkout's .env into the worktree -- consistent with prior memory (feedback_env_not_inline_keys: provision via cp, never inline keys) but this is the same class of friction recurring across WPs (AR1, AV4 also hit env/harness-lane gaps).

Even with .env provisioned, vitest.integration.config.ts / its setup file do not auto-load .env for the harness project -- the reviewer had to manually re-run the two AU11-touched harness test files with `node --env-file=.env` to get a real pass/fail signal. This is standing infra friction independent of AU11's changes (reviewer explicitly called it out as non-blocking but real): the harness integration lane silently no-ops to 'no key found' rather than loading the same .env the rest of verify uses.

Reviewer did not trust the builder's self-report on the harness gap -- it independently ran test:integration:harness twice (once cold, once with --env-file=.env), got 31/34 passing with all 3 codex-only failures traced to an external codex ChatGPT-account usage-limit error unrelated to AU11, and used the builtin/claude/opencode passes to live-prove the relocated services/mcp-route.ts end-to-end (Stop hook -> real /api/mcp/:token/return-status; commit_file -> MCP bridge). This closes exactly the kind of integration-proof gap compound candidate C1 tracks, and did so without asking the builder to redo work.

Of 4 judgment calls the builder flagged for reviewer attention (mcp-route reclassified descriptor-read->direct-execution; 3 extra descriptor-read allowlist entries; 5 dead files+exports kept via knip ignore; deletion of app-runtime-service-ownership.test.ts), the reviewer ruled 3 of 4 correct and only 1 (the knip masking) incorrect. Builder's self-flagging of uncertain calls worked as intended -- surfaced the real defect instead of hiding it, and the 3 correct calls didn't cost a rework cycle.

Fixing F1 (deleting the 5 masked files) cascaded: lifting the knip ignores unmasked 17 more dead exports on otherwise-live files (superseded duplicates of @hyperidle/shared types in knowledge/types.ts, plus a never-wired setKnowledgeEventBus seam whose @lore comment falsely claimed app.ts still used it). The single-file masking defect had non-obvious blast radius once the guardrail (knip.json ignore) was removed -- worth noting for cost estimation: a 'delete 5 files' fix instruction actually touched 9 files including 3 test files and required per-name caller verification for ~19 exports.

Cost/cycle summary for AU11: 8 commits total (guard-red, 3 move commits, boot-split, docs+knip, 1 review-fix commit, 2 attestation commits), 2 critique rounds (both closed round 2, no re-open), 2 code-review rounds (round 1 WARNING -> round 2 DONE), zero reverts/force-pushes, full verify green at every major commit. The single rework cycle (F1 dead-code masking) was caught pre-ship by review, not by CI or a later WP -- the gate worked as designed for a 67-file mechanical dissolution.
